title: Software
content:
Engineer Capers Jones writes that "computers and software are making profound changes to every aspect of human life: education, work, warfare, entertainment, medicine, law, and everything else". It has become ubiquitous in everyday life in developed countries. In many cases, software augments the functionality of existing technologies such as household appliances and elevators. Software also spawned entirely new technologies such as the Internet, video games, mobile phones, and GPS. New methods of communication, including email, forums, blogs, microblogging, wikis, and social media, were enabled by the Internet. Massive amounts of knowledge exceeding any paper-based library are now available with a quick web search. Most creative professionals have switched to software-based tools such as [...] Completing a software project involves various forms of expertise, not just in software programmers but also testing, documentation writing, project management, graphic design, user experience, user support, marketing, and fundraising.

## Quality and security

Main articles: Software quality and Computer security [...] Software companies aim to deliver a high-quality product on time and under budget. A challenge is that software development effort estimation is often inaccurate. Software development begins by conceiving the project, evaluating its feasibility, analyzing the business requirements, and making a software design. Most software projects speed up their development by reusing or incorporating existing software, either in the form of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) or open-source software. Software quality assurance is typically a combination of manual code review by other engineers and automated software testing. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/JavaScript_code.png/250px-JavaScript_code.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JavaScript_code.png)

Software written in the [JavaScript](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript "JavaScript") language

**Software** (SW) consists of [computer programs](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_program "Computer program") that instruct the [execution](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing) "Execution (computing)") of a [computer](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer "Computer").[[1]](#cite_note-pis-p16-1) Software also includes design documents and specifications.

The history of software is closely tied to the development of digital computers in the mid-20th century. Early programs were written in the [machine language](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_language "Machine language") specific to the hardware. The introduction of [high-level programming languages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-level_programming_language "High-level programming language") in 1958 allowed for more human-readable instructions, making [software development](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development "Software development") easier and more portable across different [computer architectures](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_architecture "Computer architecture"). Software in a programming language is run through a [compiler](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler") or [interpreter](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreter_(computing) "Interpreter (computing)") to [execute](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing) "Execution (computing)") on the architecture's hardware. Over time, software has become complex, owing to developments in [networking](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_network "Computer network"), [operating systems](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_systems "Operating systems"), and [databases](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Databases "Databases").

Software can generally be categorized into two main types:

1. [operating systems](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system"), which manage hardware resources and provide services for applications
2. [application software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software "Application software"), which performs specific tasks for users

The rise of [cloud computing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") has introduced the new software delivery model [software as a service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service") (SaaS). In SaaS, applications are hosted by a [provider](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_service_provider "Application service provider") and [accessed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP "HTTP") over the [Internet](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet "Internet").

The process of developing software involves several stages. The stages include [software design](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_design "Software design"), [programming](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming "Computer programming"), [testing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_testing "Software testing"), [release](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle "Software release life cycle"), and [maintenance](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_maintenance "Software maintenance"). [Software quality assurance](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_quality_assurance "Software quality assurance") and [security](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_security "Information security") are critical aspects of software development, as [bugs](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_bug "Computer bug") and [security vulnerabilities](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulnerability_(computing) "Vulnerability (computing)") can lead to system failures and security breaches. Additionally, legal issues such as software licenses and intellectual property rights play a significant role in the distribution of software products.

## History

Main article: [History of software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_software "History of software")

The first use of the word *software* to describe computer programs is credited to mathematician [John Wilder Tukey](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Tukey "John Tukey") in 1958.[[2]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJones201419,_22-2)[[3]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy20212-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) The first programmable computers, which appeared at the end of the 1940s,[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGabbrielliMartini2023519-5) were programmed in [machine language](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_language "Machine language"). Machine language is difficult to debug and not [portable](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portability_(computing) "Portability (computing)") across different computers.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGabbrielliMartini2023520–521-6) Initially, hardware resources were more expensive than [human resources](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_resources "Human resources").[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGabbrielliMartini2023522-7) As programs became complex, [programmer productivity](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programmer_productivity "Programmer productivity") became the bottleneck. The introduction of [high-level programming languages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-level_programming_language "High-level programming language") in 1958 [hid](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstraction_(computing) "Abstraction (computing)") the details of the hardware and expressed the underlying [algorithms](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm "Algorithm") into the code.[[8]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGabbrielliMartini2023521-8)[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy20211-9) Early languages include [Fortran](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortran "Fortran"), [Lisp](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisp_(programming_language) "Lisp (programming language)"), and [COBOL](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COBOL "COBOL").[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy20211-9)

## Types

See also: [Software categories](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_categories "Software categories")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Operating_system_placement_%28software%29.svg/250px-Operating_system_placement_%28software%29.svg.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Operating_system_placement_(software).svg)

A diagram showing how the [user](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_(computing) "User (computing)") interacts with [application software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software "Application software") on a typical [desktop computer](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desktop_computer "Desktop computer"). The application software layer interfaces with the [operating system](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system"), which in turn communicates with the [hardware](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware "Computer hardware"). The arrows indicate information flow.

There are two main types of software:

* [Operating systems](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") are "the [layer of software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstraction_layer "Abstraction layer") that manages a computer's resources for its users and their [applications](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software "Application software")".[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20146-10) There are three main purposes that an operating system fulfills:[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20147-11)
  + Allocating resources between different applications, deciding when they will receive [central processing unit](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_processing_unit "Central processing unit") (CPU) time or space in [memory](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_memory "Computer memory").[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20147-11)
  + Providing an interface that abstracts the details of accessing [hardware](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware "Computer hardware") details (like physical memory) to make things easier for programmers.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20147-11)[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETanenbaumBos20235-12)
  + Offering common services, such as an interface for accessing network and disk devices. This enables an application to be run on different hardware without needing to be rewritten.[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20147,_9,_13-13)
* [Application software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software "Application software") runs on top of the operating system and uses the computer's resources to perform a task.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonDahlin20146–7-14) There are many different types of application software because the range of tasks that can be performed with modern computers is so large.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJones2014121-15) Applications account for most software[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy202166-16) and require the [environment](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_environment "Operating environment") provided by an operating system, and often other applications, in order to function.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy202172-17)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Comparison_of_on-premise%2C_IaaS%2C_PaaS%2C_and_SaaS.png/960px-Comparison_of_on-premise%2C_IaaS%2C_PaaS%2C_and_SaaS.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Comparison_of_on-premise,_IaaS,_PaaS,_and_SaaS.png)

Comparison of on-premise hardware and software, [infrastructure as a service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure_as_a_service "Infrastructure as a service") (IaaS), [platform as a service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_as_a_service "Platform as a service") (PaaS), and [software as a service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service") (SaaS)

Software can also be categorized by how it is [deployed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_deployment "Software deployment"). Traditional applications are purchased with a perpetual [license](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_license "Software license") for a specific version of the software, downloaded, and run on hardware belonging to the purchaser.[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022386-18) The rise of [the Internet](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Internet "The Internet") and [cloud computing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") enabled a new model, [software as a service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service") (SaaS),[[19]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECampbell-KellyGarcia-Swartz2015156–157-19) in which the provider hosts the software (usually built on top of rented [infrastructure](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure_as_a_service "Infrastructure as a service") or [platforms](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_as_a_service "Platform as a service"))[[20]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERosatiLynn202023-20) and provides the use of the software to customers, often in exchange for a [subscription fee](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subscription_fee "Subscription fee").[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022386-18) By 2023, SaaS products—which are usually delivered via a [web application](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application "Web application")—had become the primary method that companies deliver applications.[[21]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWatt20234-21)

## Development and maintenance

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Traditional_software_development_life_cycle_diagram.png/960px-Traditional_software_development_life_cycle_diagram.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Traditional_software_development_life_cycle_diagram.png)

Diagram for a traditional [software development life cycle](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development_life_cycle "Software development life cycle") from 1988. The numbers represent the typical cost of each phase.

Software companies aim to deliver a high-quality product on time and under budget. A challenge is that [software development effort estimation](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development_effort_estimation "Software development effort estimation") is often inaccurate.[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan20227-22) [Software development](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development "Software development") begins by conceiving the project, evaluating its feasibility, analyzing the business requirements, and making a [software design](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_design "Software design").[[23]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan20225-23)[[24]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDooley20171-24) Most software projects speed up their development by [reusing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_reuse "Software reuse") or incorporating existing software, either in the form of [commercial off-the-shelf](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_off-the-shelf "Commercial off-the-shelf") (COTS) or [open-source software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software").[[25]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan202218,_110–111-25)[[26]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy202143,_76-26) [Software quality assurance](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_quality_assurance "Software quality assurance") is typically a combination of manual [code review](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_review "Code review") by other engineers[[27]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022117–118-27) and automated [software testing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_testing "Software testing"). Due to time constraints, testing cannot cover all aspects of the software's intended functionality, so developers often focus on the most critical functionality.[[28]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan202254-28) [Formal methods](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_method "Formal method") are used in some safety-critical systems to prove the correctness of code,[[29]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022267-29) while [user acceptance testing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_acceptance_testing "User acceptance testing") helps to ensure that the product meets customer expectations.[[30]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan202220-30) There are a variety of [software development methodologies](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development_methodologies "Software development methodologies"), which vary from completing all steps in order to concurrent and iterative models.[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan20229-31) Software development is driven by [requirements](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_requirements "Software requirements") taken from prospective users, as opposed to maintenance, which is driven by events such as a change request.[[32]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETripathyNaik201426-32)

Frequently, software is [released](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle "Software release life cycle") in an incomplete state when the development team runs out of time or funding.[[33]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReifer201222-33) Despite [testing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_testing "Software testing") and [quality assurance](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_quality_assurance "Software quality assurance"), virtually all software contains [bugs](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_bug "Software bug") where the system does not work as intended. Post-release [software maintenance](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_maintenance "Software maintenance") is necessary to remediate these bugs when they are found and keep the software working as the environment changes over time.[[34]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETripathyNaik20144,_27-34) New features are often added after the release. Over time, the level of maintenance becomes increasingly restricted before being cut off entirely when the product is withdrawn from the market.[[35]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETripathyNaik201489-35) As software [ages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_aging "Software aging"), it becomes known as [legacy software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy_software "Legacy software") and can remain in use for decades, even if there is no one left who knows how to fix it.[[36]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy20213-36) Over the lifetime of the product, software maintenance is estimated to comprise 75 percent or more of the total development cost.[[37]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVarga20186-37)[[38]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUlziit_''et_al.''2015764-38)

Completing a software project involves various forms of expertise, not just in [software programmers](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_programmer "Software programmer") but also testing, documentation writing, [project management](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_project_management "Software project management"), [graphic design](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphic_design "Graphic design"), [user experience](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_experience "User experience"), user support, [marketing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing "Marketing"), and fundraising.[[39]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETuckerMorellide_Silva20117-39)[[40]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStull201824–25-40)[[24]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDooley20171-24)

## Quality and security

Main articles: [Software quality](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_quality "Software quality") and [Computer security](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_security "Computer security")

[Software quality](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_quality "Software quality") is defined as meeting the stated requirements as well as customer expectations.[[41]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGalin20183-41) Quality is an overarching term that can refer to a code's correct and efficient behavior, its reusability and [portability](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porting "Porting"), or the ease of modification.[[42]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGalin201826-42) It is usually more cost-effective to build quality into the product from the beginning rather than try to add it later in the development process.[[43]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan202268,_117-43) Higher quality code will reduce lifetime cost to both suppliers and customers as it is more reliable and [easier to maintain](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maintainability "Maintainability").[[44]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan20223,_268-44)[[45]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVarga201812-45) Software failures in [safety-critical systems](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety-critical_system "Safety-critical system") may result in serious harm, including injury or death.[[44]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan20223,_268-44) By some estimates, the cost of poor quality software can be as high as 20 to 40 percent of sales.[[46]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022119-46) Despite developers' goal of delivering a product that works entirely as intended, virtually all software contains bugs.[[47]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAblonBogart20171-47)

The rise of the Internet also greatly increased the need for [computer security](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_security "Computer security") as it enabled malicious actors to conduct [cyberattacks](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberattack "Cyberattack") remotely.[[48]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECampbell-KellyGarcia-Swartz2015164-48)[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022266-49) If a bug creates a security risk, it is called a [vulnerability](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulnerability_(computing) "Vulnerability (computing)").[[50]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAblonBogart20172-50)[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDaswaniElbayadi202125-51) [Software patches](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patch "Software patch") are often released to fix identified vulnerabilities, but those that remain unknown ([zero days](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-day_(computing) "Zero-day (computing)")) as well as those that have not been patched are still liable for exploitation.[[52]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDaswaniElbayadi202126–27-52) Vulnerabilities vary in their ability to be [exploited](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exploit_(computer_security) "Exploit (computer security)") by malicious actors,[[50]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAblonBogart20172-50) and the actual risk is dependent on the nature of the vulnerability as well as the value of the surrounding system.[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaberHibbert20185–6-53) Although some vulnerabilities can only be used for [denial of service](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial_of_service "Denial of service") attacks that compromise a system's availability, others allow the attacker to [inject](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_injection "Code injection") and run their own code (called [malware](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malware "Malware")), without the user being aware of it.[[50]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAblonBogart20172-50) To thwart cyberattacks, all software in the system must be designed to withstand and recover from external attack.[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022266-49) Despite efforts to ensure security, a significant fraction of computers are infected with malware.[[54]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKitchinDodge201137-54)

## Encoding and execution

### Programming languages

Main article: [Programming language](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language "Programming language")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/C_Hello_World_Program.png/330px-C_Hello_World_Program.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:C_Hello_World_Program.png)

The [source code](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_code "Source code") for a computer program in [C](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language) "C (programming language)"). The gray lines are [comments](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comment_(computer_programming) "Comment (computer programming)") that explain the program to humans. When [compiled](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiled "Compiled") and [run](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing) "Execution (computing)"), it will output "[Hello, world!](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/)".

Programming languages are the format in which software is written. Since the 1950s, thousands of different programming languages have been invented; some have been in use for decades, while others have fallen into disuse.[[55]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy2021117-55) Some definitions classify [machine code](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_code "Machine code")—the exact instructions directly implemented by the hardware—and [assembly language](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assembly_language "Assembly language")—a more human-readable alternative to machine code whose statements can be translated one-to-one into machine code—as programming languages.[[56]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy2021118–120-56) Programs written in the [high-level programming languages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-level_programming_languages "High-level programming languages") used to create software share a few main characteristics: knowledge of machine code is not necessary to write them, they can be [ported](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ported "Ported") to other computer systems, and they are more concise and human-readable than machine code.[[57]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy2021118–119-57) They must be both human-readable and capable of being translated into unambiguous instructions for computer hardware.[[58]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKitchinDodge201126-58)

### Compilation, interpretation, and execution

The invention of high-level programming languages was simultaneous with the [compilers](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler") needed to translate them automatically into machine code.[[59]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy2021121-59) Most programs do not contain all the resources needed to run them and rely on external [libraries](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_library "Software library"). Part of the compiler's function is to link these files in such a way that the program can be executed by the hardware. Once compiled, the program can be saved as an [object file](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_file "Object file") and the [loader](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loader_(computing) "Loader (computing)") (part of the operating system) can take this saved file and [execute](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing) "Execution (computing)") it as a [process](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Process "Process") on the computer hardware.[[60]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETracy2021122–123-60) Some programming languages use an [interpreter](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreter_(computing) "Interpreter (computing)") instead of a compiler. An interpreter converts the program into machine code at [run time](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing) "Execution (computing)"), which makes them 10 to 100 times slower than compiled programming languages.[[61]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022375-61)[[62]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESebesta201228-62)

## Legal issues

### Liability

Main article: [Software product liability](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_product_liability "Software product liability")

Software is often released with the knowledge that it is incomplete or contains bugs.[*[citation needed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Purchasers knowingly buy it in this state,[*[citation needed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] which has led to a legal regime where [liability](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_liability "Product liability") for software products is significantly curtailed compared to other products.[[63]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKitchinDodge201136–37-63)

### Licenses

Main articles: [Software license](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_license "Software license") and [Software copyright](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_copyright "Software copyright")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Cube_in_Blender_Editor.jpg/250px-Cube_in_Blender_Editor.jpg)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cube_in_Blender_Editor.jpg)

[Blender](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blender_(software) "Blender (software)"), a [free software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_software "Free software") program

Since the mid-1970s, software and its source code have been protected by [copyright law](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_law "Copyright law") that vests the owner with the exclusive right to copy the code. The underlying ideas or algorithms are not protected by copyright law, but are sometimes treated as a [trade secret](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_secret "Trade secret") and concealed by such methods as [non-disclosure agreements](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-disclosure_agreement "Non-disclosure agreement").[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022394–396-64) A [software copyright](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_copyright "Software copyright") is often owned by the person or company that financed or made the software (depending on their contracts with employees or [contractors](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_contracting_in_the_United_States "Independent contracting in the United States") who helped to write it).[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022403-65) Some software is in the [public domain](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_domain "Public domain") and has no restrictions on who can use it, copy or share it, or modify it; a notable example is software written by the [United States Government](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States").[*[citation needed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] [Free and open-source software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open-source_software "Free and open-source software") also allow free use, sharing, and modification, perhaps with a few specified conditions.[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022403-65) The use of some software is governed by an agreement ([software license](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_license "Software license")) written by the copyright holder and imposed on the user. [Proprietary software](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proprietary_software "Proprietary software") is usually sold under a restrictive license that limits its use and sharing.[[66]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022394,_404-66) Some free software licenses require that modified versions must be released under the same license, which prevents the software from being sold or distributed under proprietary restrictions.[[67]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELanger201644–45-67)

### Patents

Main articles: [Software patent](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent "Software patent") and [Software patent debate](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent_debate "Software patent debate")

[Patents](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patent "Patent") give an inventor an exclusive, time-limited license for a novel product or process.[[68]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022395-68) Ideas about what software could accomplish are not protected by law and concrete implementations are instead covered by [copyright law](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_law "Copyright law"). In some countries, a requirement for the claimed invention to have an effect on the physical world may also be part of the requirements for a software patent to be held valid.[[69]](#cite_note-69) [Software patents](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent "Software patent") have been [historically controversial](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent_debate "Software patent debate"). Before the 1998 case *[State Street Bank & Trust Co. v. Signature Financial Group, Inc.](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Street_Bank_&_Trust_Co._v._Signature_Financial_Group,_Inc. "State Street Bank & Trust Co. v. Signature Financial Group, Inc.")*, software patents were generally not recognized in the United States. In that case, the [Supreme Court](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") decided that business processes could be patented.[[70]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJones201419-70) Patent applications are complex and costly, and lawsuits involving patents can drive up the cost of products.[[71]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022398-71) Unlike copyrights, patents generally only apply in the jurisdiction where they were issued.[[72]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Regan2022399-72)

"Computer-aided design"), [3D modeling](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_modeling "3D modeling"), digital [image editing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_editing "Image editing"), and [computer animation](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_animation "Computer animation").[[73]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEManovich2013333-73) Almost every complex device is controlled by software.[[77]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJones2014xxviii-77)
